analysis.notes: A swing-era tune built on I–ii–V motion with the classic I–I7–IV–#ivdim7 walk-up in bars 5–6 (F6–F7–Bb6–Bdim7) and a I–VI7–ii–V turnaround. The bridge leans on the subdominant (Bb6) and then II7 (G7, V7/V) before the ii–V back home. Simple enough to play at a bright tempo, rich enough to practise passing diminished chords and turnarounds.

learning.why: Rhythm changes in miniature: the I–I7–IV–#ivdim7 walk-up and the I–VI–ii–V turnaround are the two most common four-bar cells in the swing repertoire.
drills: Comp four to the bar (Freddie Green style) with shells through the whole form at 144 BPM.
Loop bars 5–6 and connect F6–F7–Bb6–Bdim7 with a bass line in the thumb.
Solo using the F major scale and target the B natural over Bdim7.
Play the turnaround (F6–D7–Gm7–C7) in all twelve keys with the gym's transposition.
listen: Nat King Cole Trio — It's Only a Paper Moon (1943)
Ella Fitzgerald — Ella Fitzgerald Sings the Harold Arlen Song Book (1961)
milestones: Know the form and changes from memory
Comp shells four-to-the-bar through the form
Comp drop-2 voicings with the trio
Play a chord-tone solo over the whole form
Play the melody from memory (learn it by ear from a recording)
